entities.summary:
Terentianus, surnamed Maurus, was a Latin grammarian and writer on prosody who flourished probably at the end of the 2nd century AD.

Born in Africa, he studied rhetoric and philosophy under the tutelage of prominent scholars, including the Stoic philosopher Ptolemy.

Terentianus's most significant contribution was his development of the "Caesarian model" of Latin grammar, which emphasized the importance of correct pronunciation and pronunciation patterns.

His work, particularly his treatise on prosody, had a profound impact on the development of Latin language and literature, influencing prominent writers such as Cicero and Virgil.

Despite his importance in the literary world, Terentianus's life remains somewhat of a mystery, and his exact place of death and burial are unknown.

Terentianus's legacy can be seen in the many Latin texts that have survived to this day, including his own works, which continue to be studied and appreciated by scholars and language enthusiasts alike.
